name: Zagora
hero_subtitle: Gateway to the Sahara: palm-lined Draa Valley, the Timbuktu sign, nearby dunes and the calm rhythm of southern oasis towns.

overview.title: Welcome to Zagora — palms, caravan memory and the road to the dunes
overview.p1: Zagora sits in the Draa Valley of southern Morocco, long a staging stop on routes toward Timbuktu. Calmer than the major imperial cities, the town is framed by palm groves and the Anti-Atlas with the feel of a Saharan gateway.
overview.p2: Many travellers stop by the Timbuktu 52 days sign, walk or drive through the palm groves, head to the Tinfou dunes and spend half a day in Tamegroute for green pottery and its historic library. Amezrou and Jebel Zagora add lanes and a sunset viewpoint.
overview.p3: A stay of 2 to 4 days is ideal if you want to explore the oasis and spend a night in the desert. Summer heat rises significantly, making autumn to spring the preferred season when evenings are refreshing.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day plan for Zagora
itinerary.subtitle: Oasis and sign first, then Tamegroute or dunes, then a desert night or free day.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Stop by the sign, then get your bearings in the centre.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Walk or drive among Draa palms and earthen villages.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Climb or viewpoint for sunset over the oasis if energy allows.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Green pottery workshops and historic library south of town.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Short outing to the dunes before a desert night if desired.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Simple meal in the oasis and early night if a camp is planned.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Head toward camp or stroll through Amezrou lanes at an easy pace.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Dune time and tea, or packing and a last walk under the palms.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Desert night sky or return to town for your next leg.

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: The centre is compact; Tamegroute, Tinfou and camps require a taxi, excursion or vehicle. Agree rates before desert tracks.

bargain.title: Heat & water
bargain.desc: Summer heat is strong. Carry plenty of water, sun protection and a hat, and start early for Jebel Zagora and the dunes.

water.title: Cash & season
water.desc: Keep dirhams for taxis, guides and small stops, and book camps ahead in peak season.

q1.question: How many days in Zagora?
q1.answer: Two days cover the sign, palm groves and Tamegroute or Tinfou. Three to four days allow a desert night at an unhurried pace.

q2.question: Is Zagora only a stop to the desert?
q2.answer: Desert camps draw many visitors, while the Draa palm groves, Tamegroute, Amezrou and Jebel Zagora already offer plenty to see.

q3.question: How do I get to Zagora?
q3.answer: Most visitors travel by road from Ouarzazate (about 2.5 to 3 hours) or from Marrakech via the south.

q4.question: Best time to visit?
q4.answer: From October to April, temperatures are milder. In summer, heat can be extreme and limits daytime outings.
